description: Original johnson mod.rs with bounded correspondence models.
state: Ordered directed adjacency lists with i64 weights; at most 1024 vertices and one million edges. Returned observation is the complete Result of an i128 optional distance matrix.
cost: O(V(V+E)+V E log(E+1)) time; O(V²+V+E) storage. Heap duplicates are counted. Checked i128 arithmetic and explicit vertex/edge caps; allocator failure is not caught.
forward: Check size limits, then every target in row order. Synchronous Bellman-Ford potentials start at zero at every vertex (implicit super-source); an improvement on round V rejects a negative cycle anywhere. Transform w to w+h[u]-h[v], run lazy minimum-heap Dijkstra for each source with i128 keys, then restore d=d_prime-h[source]+h[target].
inverse: Let U be declared inputs crossed with returned observations and R the forward relation in model.md#approximant. C=U minus R includes wrong first errors, wrong values and forbidden results. This is an exact specification complement and partial source-derived model, not a measured global Rust complement. Accepted potentials satisfy h[v]<=h[u]+w for every edge. Reweighted weights are nonnegative. At successful return every diagonal is zero, absent cells mean unreachable, and finite cells are minimum walk weights.

Pre(y)={x in domain | R(x,y)} retains all compatible inputs. Outputs lose redundant edges and intermediate heap/pivot traces; errors retain all graphs sharing their first-failure condition. No unique recovery or inverse executor is claimed.
limitations: Finite evidence is not a general proof; allocation failures unmodeled.
Partial syntax excludes macro expansion and semantic resolution.
